run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T06:41:57Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on frontend-proxy coincides with a short burst of HTTP 500 responses on POST /api/checkout (first observed 06:42:15.787Z, last 06:44:17.401Z). The failing leg was checkout -> payment: checkout's oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge client spans are the only ERROR-status RPC spans on that path, while payment's own grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge server series reports no ERROR status. The payment Deployment was rolled out at 06:42:10Z: its only pod payment-55766d76b9-5frt4 was killed at 06:42:15Z, the replacement pod payment-79d86bf97f-9pm9t started its gRPC server only at 06:43:31.791Z and received its first Charge at 06:44:18.991Z, and the Deployment defines no readiness probe. That chain is supported as the cause of the alert. Separately, the flagd ConfigMap read after the incident window declares paymentFailure defaultVariant 100% and paymentUnreachable defaultVariant on; those fault-injection settings match the failure path but their values during the burst are unverified and are contradicted by successful charges from 06:45Z onward, so they remain a hypothesis. The burst was transient; the alert's recorded start (06:41:57Z) is about 18 seconds before the first observed proxy 500, and the alert rule expression was not retrievable.

claims.text: The frontend-proxy ingress STATUS_CODE_ERROR counter was 498 at 06:40:00Z, 499 at 06:42:00Z, 543 at 06:44:00Z, 583 at 06:46:00Z and 584 at 06:50:00Z, so nearly all of its growth occurred between 06:42 and 06:46Z.

frontend-proxy access logs show POST /api/checkout returning 500: the first 500 in the 06:41:00-06:43:11Z window is at 06:42:15.787Z, 39 such 500 lines appear through 06:43:10.871Z, 500s continue through 06:44:17.401Z, and a 200 response appears at 06:44:18.099Z.
The summed checkout oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge STATUS_CODE_ERROR series was 80 at 06:45:00Z and 81 at 06:50:00Z, showing checkout recorded errors on its client call to payment during this burst.

In the 06:40-07:00Z query of ERROR-status span increases, the failing path appears as checkout oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge, frontend POST, POST /api/checkout, executing api route (pages) /api/checkout and grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, and frontend-proxy ingress and router frontend egress.
The same 06:40-07:00Z error-span query returned no nonzero ERROR increase for accounting, cart, currency, email, image-provider, payment, product-catalog, quote or shipping.

The same query also returned small nonzero ERROR series on ad, fraud-detection and recommendation for flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream operations, which are different operations from the checkout->payment path.

The payment Deployment's pod template carries kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T06:42:10Z, uses image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment, and defines neither a readinessProbe nor a livenessProbe.

otel-demo events at 06:42:10-06:42:15Z are limited to the payment rollout: Deployment payment scaled the new ReplicaSet payment-79d86bf97f from 0 to 1, created pod payment-79d86bf97f-9pm9t, the old pod payment-55766d76b9-5frt4 was killed (Stopping container payment) with ReplicaSet payment-55766d76b9 SuccessfulDelete, and the old ReplicaSet was scaled from 1 to 0.

The old and new payment ReplicaSets both use image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment; payment-55766d76b9 has 0 replicas and payment-79d86bf97f has 1 replica with the 06:42:10Z restartedAt annotation.

The replacement payment pod's container started at 06:42:14Z but its log shows 'payment gRPC server started on port 8080' only at 06:43:31.791Z, and its first 'Charge request received.' line is at 06:44:18.991Z.

Checkout logs from 06:42:51.623Z through 06:44:06.602Z contain 53 '[PlaceOrder]' lines and no 'payment went through' or 'order placed' lines; from 06:45:04.860Z onward the same pod logs 'payment went through' and 'order placed' repeatedly.

Over 06:41:57-07:04:58Z, payment's own grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge series reported STATUS_CODE_ERROR as 0 while STATUS_CODE_UNSET increased (439.63), i.e. the payment application did not record ERROR status on the charges it served.

At the time of the query (07:06Z, after the incident window), the flagd-config ConfigMap declares paymentFailure defaultVariant '100%' (numeric variants 0.1 to 1) and paymentUnreachable defaultVariant 'on', alongside other fault flags that are 'off'.

Checkout charges succeeded again during the window: payment logged many 'Charge request received.' lines and checkout logged many 'payment went through'/'order placed' lines from 06:45Z through at least 06:53Z.

Because the payment container has no readiness probe, pod Ready did not wait for the gRPC listener; this is consistent with the Deployment removing the old pod at 06:42:15Z, one second after the replacement container started at 06:42:14Z, while the new application did not listen until 06:43:31.791Z.

The payment container's CPU limit of 20m may have contributed to the roughly 77-second gap between container start (06:42:14Z) and the gRPC server start (06:43:31.791Z); no CPU-throttling metric was available to confirm this.

The flagd fault-injection settings paymentFailure=100% and paymentUnreachable=on could have contributed to the Charge failures if they were being served around 06:42-06:44Z, but the ConfigMap was read after the window and its values at that time are unverified.

The currently declared paymentFailure=100% (and paymentUnreachable=on) cannot be assumed to have been in effect during the successful period: checkout and payment logs show charges succeeding from 06:45Z onward, and payment's own Charge series shows no ERROR status, so a 100% payment-failure setting is contradicted for that period.
Add a readinessProbe (and a livenessProbe) to the payment container so the payment Service does not receive traffic before the gRPC listener is up.

Avoid restarting the single payment replica without a serving standby (raise replicas or set the rolling update so the old pod is retained until the replacement app is listening), and verify why the 06:42:10Z rollout restart was issued.

gaps: change_history is not integrated, so the actor and reason for the payment Deployment restart at 06:42:10Z (kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt) are unknown.

list_prometheus_rules returned no rule named RequestErrorRate, so the alert expression and evaluation window are unknown; this leaves the about 18-second gap between the recorded alert start (06:41:57Z) and the first observed proxy 500 (06:42:15.787Z) unexplained.

The flagd containers produced no log lines in the queried window, and the flagd-config ConfigMap was read at 07:06Z after the incident; whether paymentFailure/paymentUnreachable were served during the burst could not be verified.

Jaeger searches for checkout/frontend/frontend-proxy in 06:41-07:04Z returned no traces (one retained result reported source_end_at 06:33:40Z), so the trace-level details and error messages of the failing Charge calls could not be read.

Prometheus queries for kube_deployment_status_replicas_available and kube_pod_container_status_ready in otel-demo returned no data, so payment's Ready and available-replica transitions during the rollout are unknown.
The old payment pod payment-55766d76b9-5frt4 no longer exists; its logs, termination reason and exit code could not be read.
No CPU-throttling metric was found, so the hypothesis that the 20m CPU limit slowed payment startup is unconfirmed.
next_steps: Ask the deployment owner/CI to confirm what triggered the 06:42:10Z rollout restart of Deployment payment and whether it was an intentional change.
Review the flagd demo.flagd.json values (paymentFailure=100%, paymentUnreachable=on) with the team that manages fault injection and confirm or revert them.
Test adding a readinessProbe and more than one replica for payment, and measure startup time with a higher CPU limit, before relying on this Deployment for availability.

data.relay:
connectors:
  spanmetrics:
    dimensions:
    - default: otel-demo
      name: namespace
exporters:
  clickhouse:
    endpoint: http://clickhouse-clickhouse.clickhouse.svc.cluster.local:8123
    logs_table_name: otel_demo_logs
    password: ""
    traces_table_name: otel_demo_traces
    username: default
  debug: {}
  opensearch:
    http:
      endpoint: http://opensearch-master.opensearch.svc.cluster.local:9200
      tls:
        insecure: true
    logs_index: otel-logs
    logs_index_time_format: yyyy-MM-dd
  otlp:
    endpoint: jaeger-collector.opentelemetry-collectors.svc.cluster.local:4317
    tls:
      insecure: true
  otlphttp/prometheus:
    endpoint: http://prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus.prometheus.svc.cluster.local:9090
    tls:
      insecure: true
  prometheus:
    endpoint: 0.0.0.0:8889
extensions:
  health_check:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:13133
processors:
  batch: {}
  k8sattributes:
    extract:
      metadata:
      - k8s.namespace.name
      - k8s.deployment.name
      - k8s.statefulset.name
      - k8s.daemonset.name
      - k8s.cronjob.name
      - k8s.job.name
      - k8s.node.name
      - k8s.pod.name
      - k8s.pod.uid
      - k8s.pod.start_time
    passthrough: false
    pod_association:
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.ip
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.uid
    - sources:
      - from: connection
  memory_limiter:
    check_interval: 5s
    limit_percentage: 80
    spike_limit_percentage: 25
  resource:
    attributes:
    - action: insert
      from_attribute: k8s.pod.uid
      key: service.instance.id
  resourcedetection:
    detectors:
    - env
    - system
  transform:
    error_mode: ignore
    trace_statements:
    - context: span
      statements:
      - replace_pattern(name, "\\?.*", "")
      - replace_match(name, "GET /api/products/*", "GET /api/products/{productId}")
receivers:
  httpcheck/frontend-proxy:
    targets:
    - endpoint: http://frontend-proxy:8080
  jaeger:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14250
      thrift_compact:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:6831
      thrift_http:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14268
  nginx:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: http://image-provider:8081/status
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4317
      http:
        cors:
          allowed_origins:
          - http://*
          - https://*
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4318
  postgresql:
    endpoint: postgresql:5432
    metrics:
      postgresql.blks_hit:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.blks_read:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.deadlocks:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_deleted:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_fetched:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_inserted:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_returned:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_updated:
        enabled: true
    password: [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
    tls:
      insecure: true
    username: root
  prometheus:
    config:
      scrape_configs:
      - job_name: opentelemetry-collector
        scrape_interval: 10s
        static_configs:
        - targets:
          - ${env:MY_POD_IP}:8888
  redis:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: valkey-cart:6379
    username: valkey
  zipkin:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:9411
service:
  extensions:
  - health_check
  pipelines:
    logs:
      exporters:
      - clickhouse
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resourcedetection
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
    metrics:
      exporters:
      - debug
      - prometheus
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resourcedetection
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - httpcheck/frontend-proxy
      - nginx
      - otlp
      - postgresql
      - redis
      - spanmetrics
    traces:
      exporters:
      - clickhouse
      - debug
      - otlp
      - spanmetrics
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resourcedetection
      - resource
      - transform
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
      - jaeger
      - zipkin
  telemetry:
    metrics:
      level: detailed
      readers:
      - pull:
          exporter:
            prometheus:
              host: 0.0.0.0
              port: 8888
